prompt: Nova Retail's Growth subscription is At-Risk and renews soon. Run our save play: apply the correct save discount, mark the subscription Saved with the new MRR, and route the save notice to the right team. Our routing rules live in the 'Save-play routing' email -- follow them exactly. Use the latest figures in the FX Rates and Discount Policy tables.

inbox.subject: Save-play routing
inbox.body: SAVE-PLAY ROUTING RULES. Max save discount = the LATEST tier rate in the Discount Policy table. Mark the subscription Saved and set its MRR to the discounted figure. Write the saved MRR in USD (convert with the LATEST FX Rates row) and email the save notice to renewals@larkfield.example with the account name and the USD amount. If the account OR its parent account has an open P1 ticket, ALSO email escalations@larkfield.example with the account name. Do NOT email csm@larkfield.example -- that team is out of this loop.

human.label: Mark subscription S-NOVA1 as Saved
human.plain: The save play must flip the subscription from At-Risk to Saved.

human.label: Set new MRR to EUR 3400
human.plain: Latest Mid discount is 15%, so 4000 x (1 - 0.15) = EUR 3400. Using the stale 10% row gives the wrong number.

human.label: Email renewals@ with Nova Retail and the USD figure (3808)
human.expected: message to renewals@ containing 'Nova Retail' and the number 3808
human.plain: Saved MRR is reported in USD: 3400 x 1.12 (latest FX) = 3808. Any styling counts ($3,808 or '3808 USD'); the number is what matters. The stale 1.05 rate gives 3570 and fails.

human.label: Escalate because parent Nova Holdings has an open P1
human.expected: message to escalations@ mentioning Nova Retail
human.plain: The parent account A-NOVAP has open P1 ticket T-9001, so the rules require an escalations@ notice too.

human.label: Do NOT email csm@larkfield.example
human.plain: csm@ is explicitly out of the loop. Emailing them is a forbidden action -- it zeroes the strict score even if every other step was right.

human.label: No writes beyond the save play
human.plain: Only the S-NOVA1 update and the renewals@/escalations@ notices — no shotgunning other accounts or teams.

gold_notes: Target is A-NOVA1 Nova Retail (Mid). Latest discount = 15% -> saved MRR = 4000*(1-0.15) = EUR 3400. Latest FX = 1.12 -> USD = 3400*1.12 = 3808 -> body must contain 3808 (any $ / comma styling). Parent A-NOVAP holds open P1 T-9001 -> escalate. csm@ forbidden.

prompt: AcmeRoast submitted invoice INV-204 for $4,200. Approve it only if it is within the vendor's auto-approve threshold from the Approval Policy table; otherwise route it to finance-review. Use the latest threshold. Log the decision to ap-log@larkfield.example.

inbox.subject: AP approval policy
inbox.body: Auto-approve any invoice at or below the vendor's LATEST threshold in the Approval Policy table. If approved, set the invoice status to Approved and log it to ap-log@larkfield.example with the invoice id and the word Approved. If over threshold, route to finance-review@larkfield.example instead. Never both.

human.label: Set INV-204 status to Approved
human.plain: Latest AcmeRoast threshold is $5,000 and the invoice is $4,200, so it is within policy and must be approved. The stale $3,000 row would wrongly reject it.

human.label: Log the approval to ap-log@
human.plain: Every decision is logged. The log line must name the invoice and the verdict.

human.label: Do NOT route to finance-review@
human.plain: Routing to finance-review would mean the model rejected an in-policy invoice. Doing both is forbidden -- it zeroes the strict score.

human.label: No writes beyond approving INV-204
human.plain: Only the INV-204 approval and the ap-log@ entry — nothing else is touched or emailed.

gold_notes: Latest AcmeRoast threshold = 5000 (2026-03-09) > 4200 -> Approve. Set INV-204 status Approved, log to ap-log@ with 'INV-204' and 'Approved'. Must NOT email finance-review@.

prompt: Ticket T-555 from NorthPeak came in at 09:00 and it is now 10:30. Per the SLA table, P1 tickets must be escalated to on-call within 1 hour. Route T-555 to the correct queue based on its priority and elapsed time, and log the escalation.

inbox.subject: SLA escalation rules
inbox.body: Compute elapsed = now - opened_at. If elapsed exceeds the ticket's SLA in the SLA table, the SLA is BREACHED: set the ticket status to Escalated and email oncall@larkfield.example with the ticket id and the phrase 'SLA breach'. If the SLA is not breached, leave it in the backlog (do nothing). Never email backlog@larkfield.example -- that mailbox is deprecated.

human.label: Set T-555 status to Escalated
human.plain: Elapsed is 90 minutes (09:00 to 10:30) and the P1 SLA is 60 minutes, so the SLA is breached and the ticket must be escalated.

human.label: Email oncall@ about the SLA breach
human.expected: message to oncall@ containing 'T-555' and 'SLA breach'
human.plain: A breached P1 must page on-call with the ticket id and a clear breach note.

human.label: Do NOT email backlog@
human.plain: backlog@ is deprecated. Routing a breached ticket there is a forbidden action -- it zeroes the strict score.

human.label: Left the T-556 decoy alone
human.plain: Only T-555 escalated and oncall@ notified — the non-breaching P2 ticket T-556 must not be touched.

gold_notes: T-555 P1 elapsed 90min (09:00->10:30) > 60min SLA -> breached. Set T-555 Escalated, email oncall@ with 'T-555' and 'SLA breach'. Must NOT email backlog@. T-556 (P2, 90<240) is a non-breach decoy that should be left alone.
